newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Workers threaten to picket handover ceremony.
newsitem.headline: Workers threaten to picket handover ceremony.

text.p: Workers who built the Hong Kong Convention Centre extension, spectacular site of the colony's official return to China, complained on Wednesday they had not been paid and threatened to picket the historic ceremony.
About 40 labourers who worked on the gull-winged centre, where Britain's Prince Charles is to hand back Hong Kong to China's President Jiang Zemin on Monday, gathered at the site to demand back pay.

They were barred from crossing a bridge to the HK$4.8 billion (US$620 million) building, on an artificial island in Hong Kong harbour, since they had completed their jobs and no longer had entry permits.
"We gave our sweat but got no money," they chanted in the searing summer heat along the Wanchai waterfront. "We finished the job on time, but our pay is late."
Union organiser Wong Ying Yu said the group represented 200 workers who were owed some HK$10 million (US$1.3 million) for interior painting, panelling and glass works.
If contractors refused to meet them, he said, they could be back at midnight of June 30, the time of a glamorous handover ceremony in the Grand Foyer overlooking Hong Kong harbour.
"While they're all in there, we might be out here," Wong said.
There was no immediate comment from the contractor.
